_comment: Hard design rules — finish compatibility, NKBA clearances, plumbing rough-in matching. These are constraints, not preferences. The agent cites them when they limit a choice ('matte black faucet, since you committed matte black hardware throughout' or 'we'd need 16in clearance from the toilet centerline — this vanity is too wide').

matte_black.voice_note: matte black is the universal neutral — pairs with anything, never clashes

polished_chrome.voice_note: polished chrome wants warm partners — brass or aged bronze — never another cool polished metal in the same room

brushed_nickel.voice_note: brushed nickel reads softer than chrome — pair with warm brushed brass, not its polished cousin

polished_nickel.voice_note: polished nickel is the upmarket alternative to chrome — same temperature, slightly warmer. Same rule: don't mix with chrome.

brushed_brass.voice_note: brushed brass goes with everything cool (chrome, brushed nickel) AND with matte black

polished_brass.voice_note: polished brass is the boldest finish — works as a single accent against polished nickel or chrome, but never with its own family

aged_bronze.voice_note: oil-rubbed bronze / aged bronze pairs warmly with brushed brass; can sit alongside matte black

matte_gold.voice_note: matte gold reads as a softer brass — modern. Mixes well with matte black, polished chrome, or as a single accent

rules: Pick one metal as the dominant (60-70% of metal mass) — usually the faucet + showerhead family.
Add at most ONE accent metal — typically the mirror frame, vanity light, or hardware pulls.
Never mix two finishes of the same color family — polished + brushed nickel reads as a design mistake.
Mix temperature (one warm + one cool) is the safest two-metal pairing.
Matte black is a neutral — it pairs with all other finishes.

nkba_clearances_cm._comment: From NKBA Bath Planning Guidelines (2014/2019). Used by the agent to validate placements against the user's bathroom_configuration.

plumbing_rough_in._comment: Mechanical compatibility — never a preference. Faucet hole count must match sink, toilet rough-in must match floor. The agent enforces this as a hard constraint.

faucet_hole_count.wall_mount: no sink holes; wall plumbing required
